feature.name: Pricing Change
feature.description: Move from the current tiers of $0 limited use case and $20 full access to $20 full access with limits on total discounts and $50 full access with no limits.

executiveSummary: Fly Upsell & Cross Sell is considering a pricing change that replaces the free limited tier and $20 full-access tier with a $20 limited-discount tier and a $50 unlimited-discount tier. The product targets Shopify Advanced and Plus merchants that use bundles, BOGO, quantity breaks, free gifts, and cross-sells to raise average order value. The supplied raw bundle shows three competitor inputs: Rapi, Fast Bundle, and KACHING KACHING. Rapi is a small but growing Shopify bundling app with 8 employees and 100% year-over-year headcount growth. Fast Bundle is an established Shopify bundling app founded in 2020 with a stable 5-person team. KACHING KACHING appears to be a mismatch for a Shopify bundling competitor and is a public company with 1001-5000 employees. The personas indicate that BFCM and promotion-heavy merchants have strong seasonal and campaign-driven discount needs, while efficient and low-change merchants are cost-sensitive and may resist upgrading. The company has 9k MRR, 70% margins, $8 revenue per merchant per month, $4 CAC, 4-month retention, $40 average LTV, zero burn, and 18 months of runway. The pricing change can improve ARPU and LTV if it converts high-usage merchants to the $50 plan, but it also risks churn among existing $20 full-access merchants and may increase support queries.

marketSignals.signal: Direct bundling competitors are small teams, but at least one is growing quickly.
marketSignals.evidence: Rapi has 8 employees, 33.3% six-month headcount growth, and 100% year-over-year headcount growth. Fast Bundle has 5 employees and flat headcount over the same periods.
marketSignals.implicationForFeature: The pricing change should be simple to communicate and support with a small team. A $50 unlimited tier may be easier to sell and support than complex usage-based pricing.
marketSignals.source: rawBundle.enrichResult headcount for company ids 16402024 and 3646182

marketSignals.signal: Competitor search visibility competes with broad e-commerce platforms and bundle alternatives.
marketSignals.evidence: Fast Bundle organic SEO competitors include widebundle.com, keficommerce.com, discounty.ai, bogos.io, and simplebundles.com. Rapi organic SEO competitors include wix.com, hubspot.com, mailchimp.com, oberlo.com, and bigcommerce.com.
marketSignals.implicationForFeature: Pricing pages and upgrade prompts need to convert existing merchants because discovery is contested. The $50 unlimited plan should be positioned around avoiding discount interruptions, not just more features.
marketSignals.source: rawBundle.enrichResult competitors.organic_seo for company ids 3646182 and 16402024

marketSignals.signal: BFCM and seasonal campaigns create concentrated high-usage periods.
marketSignals.evidence: Persona The BFCM Campaign Power User expects a significant temporary increase in discount activity, needs to test and deploy multiple campaign variations, and cannot afford discount interruptions during peak shopping days.
marketSignals.implicationForFeature: A $50 no-limits tier directly addresses a seasonal upgrade trigger. Messaging should emphasize unlimited discount usage during Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

marketSignals.signal: Promotion-heavy merchants view discount limits as friction.
marketSignals.evidence: Persona The Promotion Strategist runs bundles, cross-sells, quantity breaks, and free gift promotions throughout the year and sees usage limits as friction when expanding successful campaigns.
marketSignals.implicationForFeature: The $50 full-access no-limits plan fits merchants with a deliberate promotional calendar. The $20 limited-discount plan creates a natural upgrade path when campaigns scale.

marketSignals.signal: Cost-sensitive merchants may not upgrade and may resist new limits on the $20 plan.
marketSignals.evidence: Persona The Efficient Small-Scale Merchant has little friction with the current $20 plan, does not need unlimited discount usage, and is sensitive to recurring software costs. Persona The Stable, Low-Change Merchant does not want to change a working setup and may perceive a pricing change as unnecessary complexity.
marketSignals.implicationForFeature: Adding discount limits to the $20 plan risks churn or negative sentiment among existing full-access customers. Migration and communication planning is required.

marketSignals.signal: Current unit economics are thin, so ARPU expansion is material.
marketSignals.evidence: MRR is 9k USD, margin is 70%, burn is 0, revenue per merchant per month is $8, CAC is $4, retention is 4 months, average LTV is $40, and runway is 18 months.
marketSignals.implicationForFeature: Moving merchants from $8 average revenue toward $20 or $50 per month could improve unit economics, but higher churn from a pricing change could offset gains given the short 4-month retention.

marketSignals.signal: The pricing change is expected to increase support queries.
marketSignals.evidence: Expected resource consumption lists 1 engineer at 20% occupancy and support team at 20% because more queries will come along for pricing.
marketSignals.implicationForFeature: Support macros, pricing FAQs, and upgrade/downgrade flows should be prepared before launch to protect retention.

gapsAndOpportunities: No competitor pricing data is present in the raw bundle, so the $20 limited and $50 unlimited tiers cannot be benchmarked against Rapi, Fast Bundle, or any valid Kaching bundle product.
The free $0 limited-use tier appears to be removed or changed, creating an opportunity to convert free users to the $20 plan but also a risk that free users churn.
The $50 no-limits plan is a clear upgrade path for BFCM and Promotion Strategist personas who need unlimited discount usage during peak campaigns.
The $20 plan with discount limits can act as a usage-based upgrade trigger if the product surfaces limit status clearly and prompts upgrades before campaigns are interrupted.
The expected implementation resource is 1 engineer at 20% and support at 20%, which is low relative to the $10,000 financial threshold stated in productData.
Competitor SEO data suggests that bundle-related search is contested by adjacent tools and platforms, so pricing launch messaging should include comparison and migration content.
The KACHING KACHING match appears to be a false positive for a Shopify bundling competitor, leaving a gap in understanding the actual Kaching Bundles product.
risks: Existing $20 full-access customers may churn or complain if their plan gains discount limits without grandfathering or clear value justification.
The Efficient Small-Scale Merchant and Stable Low-Change Merchant personas are explicitly sensitive to recurring software costs and may reject the $50 plan.
The $50 price point is 6.25x the current $8 average revenue per merchant per month, so sales and support must clearly demonstrate value to justify the increase.
Retention is only 4 months and average LTV is $40, so any churn caused by the pricing change can quickly erode LTV gains from higher-tier upgrades.
BFCM is seasonal. Merchants may upgrade for BFCM and downgrade or cancel after the season, reducing annualized revenue per account.
Support load is expected to rise by 20% for pricing queries, which may strain a team of 4 unless documentation and self-service are prepared.
Competitors may respond with simpler or lower-priced unlimited plans, but the raw data does not include competitor pricing to assess this risk quantitatively.
The Kaching Bundles competitive picture is unreliable because the raw bundle matched KACHING KACHING, a public company with 1001-5000 employees and no recorded bundle-app positioning.
No customer usage distribution is provided, so it is unknown how many merchants would hit the $20 discount limit and upgrade to $50.
No job postings data was retrieved because the job_search query failed, limiting visibility into competitor hiring and expansion plans.
dataLimitations: The job_search tool failed with a filter condition error, so no job postings were analyzed for competitors or the company.
No pricing data for Rapi, Fast Bundle, or any valid Kaching bundle product is present in the raw data.
No Shopify App Store install counts, review counts, ratings, or revenue estimates are provided for any competitor.
Kaching Bundles was matched to KACHING KACHING, a Public Company with 1001-5000 employees; this is likely a false positive and does not clearly represent a Shopify bundling app.
Funding data is null for Rapi and KACHING KACHING, and Fast Bundle shows zero funding rounds and zero total investment.
No internal data is provided on current free-tier usage, discount usage distribution, upgrade rates, downgrade rates, or churn by plan.
No forecast is provided for the revenue impact of moving from $0/$20 to $20/$50.
Expected resource consumption provides percentages but no fully loaded labor cost, so budget fit against the $10,000 threshold cannot be precisely calculated.
Persona descriptions are qualitative and may not represent actual customer segments or willingness to pay.
Competitor headcount data is based on Crustdata snapshots and may lag actual hiring or contractor usage.
Geography is listed as worldwide, but competitor headcount data is concentrated in specific countries and may not reflect global competitive intensity.
